title: China's Mass-Produced Bronze Crossbows
hook: 2,000 years ago, Han Dynasty armories mass-produced precision bronze triggers.

scenes.text: Two thousand years before the Industrial Revolution, the Han Dynasty of China pioneered precision mass-produced weapon components.
scenes.imagePrompt: Ancient Han Dynasty stone imperial armory courtyard with stacked timber weapon crates and military banners under sunny skies. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Two thousand years before the Industrial Revolution, the Han Dynasty of China pioneered precision mass-produced weapon components.

scenes.text: Their core infantry weapon was the repeating and heavy crossbow, powered by a three-piece cast bronze trigger mechanism.
scenes.imagePrompt: Intricately cast ancient bronze crossbow trigger lock mechanism showing sear lever, tumbler, and trigger hook on a workbench. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Their core infantry weapon was the repeating and heavy crossbow, powered by a three-piece cast bronze trigger mechanism.

scenes.text: Crafted in state foundries using standardized ceramic molds, the parts were completely interchangeable between hundreds of thousands of weapons.
scenes.imagePrompt: Foundry bronze casting table with clay mold halves, bronze filing tools, and finished trigger locks awaiting inspection. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Crafted in state foundries using standardized ceramic molds, the parts were completely interchangeable between hundreds of thousands of weapons.

scenes.text: If a soldier's trigger broke on the northern frontier, an armorer replaced the sear pin in seconds without custom metal filing.
scenes.imagePrompt: Fortress watchtower on the Han Great Wall of China overlooking misty northern frontier mountains under morning light. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: If a soldier's trigger broke on the northern frontier, an armorer replaced the sear pin in seconds without custom metal filing.

scenes.text: The trigger was so smooth that peasant conscripts required only three weeks of drill to pierce heavy nomad cavalry armor at two hundred paces.

scenes.voicedText: The trigger was so smooth that peasant conscripts required only three weeks of drill to pierce heavy nomad cavalry armor at two hundred paces.

scenes.text: China invented standardized interchangeable parts two millennia before Eli Whitney! Did you know about ancient Han technology?
